nb: World's first and largest spaceport — launched Sputnik 1 and Yuri Gagarin. Home of Soyuz crewed flights.
Northern military cosmodrome — historically the single most-used launch site in the world. Soyuz and Angara.
Russia's newest spaceport in the Far East, built to reduce reliance on Baikonur.
Russia's oldest rocket range — mostly missile and sounding-rocket work, plus small orbital launches.
America's busiest launch range — Mercury, Gemini, Atlas, Delta and today's Falcon 9 fly from here.
The Moonport — Saturn V, the Space Shuttle, Falcon Heavy and Artemis all launch from pads 39A/39B.
US west-coast range for polar and Sun-synchronous orbits — spy satellites, Falcon 9, Firefly.
Virginia range for Antares, Minotaur and thousands of sounding rockets; hosts the MARS commercial pads.
Kodiak Island site for polar launches — small launchers and missile-defence tests.
SpaceX's Texas test-and-launch site for Starship, the largest rocket ever built.
Europe's spaceport, just 5° from the equator — Ariane, Vega and (formerly) Soyuz.
Arctic launch site for sounding rockets, now developing an orbital spaceport for small rockets.
Sub-Arctic Swedish range for sounding rockets and balloons, expanding toward orbital launch.
Shetland Islands site — the UK's first licensed vertical-launch orbital spaceport.
China's oldest base and only crewed-launch site — Shenzhou and the first Chinese satellite.
High-altitude Shanxi base for polar and Sun-synchronous orbits — weather and remote-sensing.
China's gateway to high orbit — communications satellites and the Beidou constellation.
China's newest, coastal spaceport — heavy Long March 5, lunar, Mars and space-station launches.
India's spaceport — PSLV and GSLV, Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan flew from here.
India's first launch site, on the magnetic equator — sounding rockets for atmospheric science.
Japan's largest launch complex on a scenic southern island — H-IIA, H-IIB and the new H3.
Hillside site for solid-fuel rockets — Japan's first satellite and today's Epsilon.
The world's first private orbital launch site — Rocket Lab's Electron flies from the Māhia Peninsula.
South Korea's spaceport — home of the domestically built Nuri (KSLV-II) rocket.
Israel launches its Shavit rockets westward over the Mediterranean — a rare retrograde orbit.
Iran's orbital launch site for the Safir and Simorgh rockets.
Tongchang-ri site — North Korea's satellite launches on the Unha and Chollima rockets.
Near-equatorial coastal range in northern Brazil, now hosting commercial small-launch operators.
Commercial equatorial spaceport in the Northern Territory — hosted NASA suborbital launches in 2022.
Vast historic range — Australia's WRESAT satellite launched here in 1967; one of the largest land ranges on Earth.
The US civil space agency's HQ in Washington, D.C. — sets policy for human spaceflight, science and aeronautics.
Paris HQ of the 22-member European Space Agency.
Moscow HQ of Russia's state space corporation.
Beijing HQ overseeing China's civil space programme, with mission control and CAST nearby.
Antariksh Bhavan, Bengaluru — HQ of the Indian Space Research Organisation.
Tokyo HQ of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency; main campus at Tsukuba.
Paris HQ of France's space agency, which co-runs the Guiana Space Centre.
Cologne HQ of the German Aerospace Center.
Swindon HQ coordinating Britain's space activities and spaceport programme.
John H. Chapman Space Centre, Longueuil — HQ of Canada's space agency (Canadarm, RADARSAT).
Pasadena centre that builds and flies NASA's robotic explorers — Voyager, the Mars rovers, and the Deep Space Network.
Houston home of Mission Control and US astronaut training — 'Houston' of Apollo and the ISS.
Darmstadt operations centre that flies ESA's satellites and deep-space probes.
The Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre outside Moscow, where cosmonauts have trained since 1960.
Mojave-desert antennas of the Deep Space Network that talk to spacecraft across the Solar System.
Southern-hemisphere Deep Space Network station — carried the Apollo 11 Moonwalk broadcast.
